title: Prior-minus-later rain slope intervals crossed zero in four insect-catch samples in Sweden and Madagascar in 2019-2020
abstract: We tested whether rain before trap placement had a stronger link to flying-insect catch than rain after collection. We used 5,756 measured catches from Sweden in 2019 and Madagascar in 2019-2020. We compared mean precipitation in the prior and later 28 days, with controls for collection weather, temperature in all windows, trap, season and duration. The four prior-minus-later slope estimates ranged from -0.050 to 0.061 log(1 + grams/day) per 5 mm/day. All 95 percent and four-test intervals included zero. The data do not establish a repeated delayed rain signal. Catches mix abundance and flight activity. One year per country, selected samples, broad weather windows and few time clusters limit inference. This is a new test of delayed rain links in an existing source dataset, not independent confirmation of the source measurements.

display.caption: Prior-minus-later 28-day precipitation slopes. Dark lines show 95 percent intervals. Pale lines show intervals adjusted for four tests. All intervals include zero.

citations.reason: We adapt the panel assembly and fixed-effect model tools. That work tested collection wet-day frequency. We test delayed precipitation with fixed 28-day windows.
